responses.text: { Malcolm Holmes top level topics }
Hello there. It's good to see a friendly face. Almost took you for a raider, I did. Name's Malcolm. Malcolm Holmes.
Don't suppose you'd care to trade? I'm missing a few essentials and- oh, screw this. Lying just ain't in my nature.
I'll tell it to you straight. I've been following you for a good bit now.
Eh? You want to talk some more?
Oh, that's right! Here, let me show you what I've got on hand.
There's not much more to tell. Get enough stars and the treasure's yours. Just watch out for some of the other people collecting them.

topics.prompt: I'd like to know more about star hunting.

responses.text: If you say so. Maybe we'll meet again.

topics.prompt: No, I have to be going.

responses.text: It started off innocently enough. I was traveling, as I often do, and happened to observe you picking up one of those blue-star caps.
You didn't show any reaction to it, so I figured you didn't know what you'd gotten your hands on.
Okay, you're a dangerous sort. I get that. But I have some information I think you'll find useful, which made me follow you for a spell.

topics.prompt: Don't follow me. You'll live longer.

responses.text: There's an old wasteland legend that says somewhere out there is a fabulous treasure from before the war.
Those caps with the blue star on them, the tale goes, are the key to that treasure. They're called Sunset Sarsaparilla Stars.

topics.prompt: What's so special about these caps?

responses.text: I had to make sure of your disposition. There's a lot of jumpy folks out there that'd shoot a man as soon as talk to him.
Now that's we're conversing, though, I can tell you what I know about those caps.

topics.prompt: Why didn't you say anything then and there?

responses.text: Fine. Just do me a favor. If you find more of those things, and plan on keeping them, watch out for a man named Allen Marks.
He's killed more than a few people to collect as many of those caps as he can, and your ignorance as to what they are won't protect you.

topics.prompt: This is getting creepy. I'm leaving, and don't follow me.

responses.text: All over the place. The easiest place to find them is unopened bottles of Sunset Sarsaparilla.
You'd think they'd all have been picked clean by now, but somehow new bottles keep appearing in the machines.
Some say it's old Festus that does it, hoping someone will finally collect enough caps to earn the treasure.
Other than bottles, you'll just have to scavenge. You can find caps in the unlikeliest of places, and blue-star caps are no exception.

topics.prompt: Where can I find more of these caps?

responses.text: Nah, I gave it up years ago. Too dangerous. And even if I did still collect them, I'd tell you the same.
There's people out there so mad with the idea of treasure that they'll attack strangers just on the suspicion that they have some of those caps.

topics.prompt: So you collect these caps too?

responses.text: No one knows. Money? Weapons? Water? It is, or maybe was, something of value, and that's enough to get people motivated.

topics.prompt: What kind of treasure are we talking about?

responses.text: It's said that the treasure is guarded by a man named Festus, and he's the one who asks for the blue-star caps.
It's also said that he's been around since the war, standing a lonely vigil, waiting for someone to come and take the treasure off his hands.
That'd make him pretty damn old, but I've met a few people in my travels who claimed they actually met him, and they weren't the lying type either.

topics.prompt: You mentioned someone named Festus. Who's that?

responses.text: No problem. If you do end up trying to collect more stars, watch out for a man named Allen Marks. He's killed several people for their stars already.

topics.prompt: Thanks for the info, but I'll be going now.
topics.label: Goodbye.
